These are semantic coverage families, not a deterministic keyword checklist. Do not repeat an accepted quote with the same normalized economic identity and do not infer a fact or absence from silence. The same literal quote may support more than one row only when each row has a materially distinct normalized predicate/object and objective effect; cosmetic relabeling is still a duplicate. Do not turn general background or adjacent technical history into production facts merely because it is economically interesting. Never use snippets, future outcomes, score, or Stage.

These interim consolidated financial statements have been\nprepared in accordance with the Korean IFRS which is effective as of March 31, 2026.\n(A) New and amended standards adopted by the Company\nThe Company applied the following amended standards for the first time for the annual reporting period commencing January\n1, 2026:\nAmendments to Korean IFRS 1109, Financial Instruments and Korean IFRS 1107, Financial Instruments: Disclosures\nThe amendments have been implemented in order to respond to questions raised in practice and include new requirements.\nThe amendments are as follows, and the adoption of the amendments does not have a significant impact on the Company’s\nconsolidated financial statements.\nThe amended standards:\n· permit derecognition of a financial liability through an electronic payment system before cash is delivered on the\nsettlement date, when specified criteria are met,\n· clarify and enhance guidance on assessing whether the contractual cash flows of financial assets consist solely of\npayments of principal and interest,\n· require disclosure of the impact of contractual terms that modify the timing and amount of contractual cash flows and the\nextent of the company’s exposure, presented by category of financial instrument, and\n· require additional disclosure regarding investments in equity instruments designated at fair value through other\ncomprehensive income.\n(B) New and amended standards not yet adopted by the Company\nThe amended accounting standards issued that are not yet effective for the annual reporting period commencing January 1,\n2026 and have not been early adopted by the Company are as follows:\nIssue of Korean IFRS 1118, Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements\nThe Korean IFRS 1118 will replace Korean IFRS 1001, Presentation of Financial Statements, and is effective for annual\nreporting periods beginning on or after January 1, 2027 with earlier application permitted. However, The Company has not\nearly adopted the new standard in preparing its interim consolidated financial statements.\nKorean IFRS 1118 introduces a more structured statement of profit or loss and requires further disaggregation of information.\nThe Company is in the process of assessing the impacts that the adoption of Korean IFRS 1118 may have on its financial\nstatements.\n- 24 -\nSamsung Electronics Co., Ltd. and its subsidiaries\nNOTES TO THE INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS\nThe expected impacts upon initial application are described below; however, the actual impacts arising from the application\nof the new standard from January 1, 2027 may differ due to the following factors:\n· The Company has not yet completed the design and assessment of changes to its processes and controls; and\n· The new accounting policies may be subject to change until the initial annual financial statements prepared under this\nnew standard are issued.\n[Structure of the Statement of Profit or Loss]\nKorean IFRS 1118 requires all income and expenses to be classified into one of five categories: operating, investing,\nfinancing, income tax, and discontinued operations. The classification of income and expenses depends on an entity’s main\nbusiness activities. The Company has assessed that certain activities, such as investing in assets or providing financing to\ncustomers, do not constitute its main business activities.\nThe application of Korean IFRS 1118 will not affect the Company’s profit for the period or net assets. However, the Company\nwill be required to present newly defined subtotals of ‘operating profit’ and ‘profit before financing and income taxes. The\noperating profit subtotal under the new standard differs from the operating profit currently presented by the Company. Based\non information currently available, the Company has performed a preliminary assessment of the potential impacts of the\napplication of Korean IFRS 1118, and the following impacts have been identified:\n· Share of net profit of associates and joint ventures is currently presented below ‘operating profit’ and above ‘financial\nincome’ and ‘financial expense’ in the statement of profit or loss. Income and expense arising from investments that are\nreported with the application of the equity method are required to be classified in the investing category under Korean\nIFRS 18. That is, share of net profit of associates and joint ventures is expected to be classified within the investing\ncategory.\n· Interest income and interest expense are currently presented as financial income and financial expense in accordance with\nthe Company’s accounting policies. Korean IFRS 1118 provides specific guidance on the classification of income and\nexpenses within the investing and financing categories. Accordingly:\n- Interest income arising from certain financial assets held by the Company (e.g., interest income on cash and cash\nequivalents) is expected to be classified within the investing category; and\n- Interest expense on certain liabilities (i.e., financial liabilities not measured at fair value through profit or loss) is\nexpected to be classified within the financing category.\n· Foreign exchange differences arising from foreign currency transactions and translation are currently presented as\nfinancial income and financial expense. Under Korean IFRS 1118, foreign exchange differences are required to be\nclassified in the same category as the income and expenses arising from the items that generated those differences. Under Korean IFRS 1118, such gains and losses should be classified in the\nsame category as the income and expenses affected by the risks that the hedging instruments are intended to manage.\nUnder Korean IFRS 1118, operating expenses are presented as separate line items using a nature, function, or mixed\npresentation format.
